_about: LIDO Event Type -> internal transaction_state. Configurable so an institution can add its own local vocabulary terms without touching code.
_why_most_terms_are_not_mapped: LIDO has no native term for a forced sale or a confiscation, and the REAO taxonomy this tool screens against is not a vocabulary LIDO carries. Only terms whose REAO equivalent is unambiguous are mapped here. Everything else is left for the record to state explicitly via PROVENA_EXT:transaction_state, and the adapter emits an ingest note naming the term it did not map, so the omission is visible rather than silent. An unmapped event is still screened: it enters as `unknown`, which the persecution-window rule treats as a transfer of unrecorded character rather than skipping it.
_direction_of_error: Under-mapping is the safe direction and over-mapping is not. `unknown` still gets screened; a wrong `restitution_erfolgt_or_vergleich` would hold an object OUT of the active queue on the strength of a term that may not mean a settled claim. That asymmetry decides every borderline case below.
review_status: Transcribed from the LIDO Event Type vocabulary (terminology.lido-schema.org) and the REAO taxonomy in src/reao_taxonomy.py. Not reviewed by a provenance researcher. The Restitution mapping is the one with queue-suppressing consequences and is the first thing a reviewer should check.
source: LIDO Terminology Event Type vocabulary, http://terminology.lido-schema.org/eventType (re-verify with scripts/fetch_lido_event_types.py).

mapped.basis: Direct equivalent; `purchase` in the REAO taxonomy is the same neutral transfer type.

Direct equivalent: a restitution event records a claim already resolved. NOTE this mapping holds the object out of the ACTIVE triage queue (see resolved_status). It is the only mapping here with that effect. Supply PROVENA_EXT:restitution_recipient_type on the same event or rule PC-008 (restitution to a state rather than to named heirs) reports itself skipped.
Direct equivalent; the term states that the character of the transfer is not recorded.

deliberately_unmapped.reason: This is the generic carrier this project maps the REAO states ONTO, not a state in itself. A record using it must say which REAO state applies; deriving one from the surrounding text is the free-text keyword inference the methodology rejects.
As above: generic, states nothing about the character of the transfer.

Not mapped to `entziehung`, which in REAO Art. 3 means a seizure by STATE act. LIDO's term does not distinguish a state seizure from a private theft, so the mapping would assert a state act the record does not establish.
Same reasoning as Looting, and further from a state act.
States that the object was lost, not how title moved.
A loan does not transfer title at all.

NOT mapped to restitution_erfolgt_or_vergleich, even though it is adjacent. Repatriation commonly names a state-to-state return, frequently in a colonial context this tool explicitly does not cover, and the mapping would suppress the object from the active queue on a term that may not mean a settled Nazi-era claim. Say so explicitly with PROVENA_EXT:transaction_state if that is what the record means.
